title: fix: recover interrupted updates after the original PR closes
body: ## What Problem This Solves Addresses #186676. A PR update can reach GitHub while its confirmation is interrupted. If the original PR then closes, recovering the same request with its original requester still authorized can create a replacement PR. Recovery can also fail after the remote branch is deleted, after the update merges, or when later local work no longer matches the accepted commit. ## User Impact Recovery records the verified accepted update against the original PR without another push or PR creation. The receipt describes the accepted update; it does not reopen the PR or claim it remains open. Later local commits, staged changes, unstaged changes and untracked files remain intact. An explicitly new publication request after closure retains its existing behavior. Publisher identity, requester authority, repository and branch checks remain in force. This contribution adds no configuration, protocol, schema or migration requirement. ## Why This Change Was Made A continued PR keeps its original body marker, while each update has its own request marker in the accepted commit. Ordinary retry checks evaluated the current branch, base and workspace before reconciling that accepted update. A closed PR, deleted remote branch or merged base could therefore send an already accepted request through fresh-publication eligibility. Both shared-worktree and repository publication now use their existing observation-only recovery owners before retrying. The shared worktree first finishes any request-owned local Git/index recovery. Reconciliation then verifies the recorded commit, tree, parent, publisher and PR identity using retained receipts. A successful observation settles the original request; a genuinely new request still follows the existing publication path. The former executor-specific shortcut is removed. ## Evidence The coordinator regression exercises real Git commits/index and SQLite admission/restart, with controlled GitHub transport for deterministic loss of confirmation. The original regression fails on frozen base `970d684a52f0d1e9f36a1e81777f1cf5c311bae4`. | Scenario | Verified result | | --- | --- | | Accepted update, lost confirmation, then original PR closes | The original request settles against the original PR without another external write | | Later local commit, staged/unstaged changes and untracked file | Saved HEAD, index and file bytes remain intact | | Original PR closes and its remote branch is deleted | Recovery does not recreate the branch or create a replacement PR | | Accepted update merges before recovery | Recovery records the accepted update instead of reporting no changes | | Repository publication backend | Recovery settles the original accepted PR without another creation POST | The local cases also verify a successful explicitly new publication request while the original PR remains closed with its accepted head. Existing revoked-authority and unavailable-observation controls remain covered. The corrected candidate has coverage for 358 selected cases across 15 affected files, with unchanged proof retained where its inputs did not change. Changed formatting, lint, affected types and per-file limits pass. The final head has a clean independent review and passing hosted CI. The runtime file passed its 23 SQLite cases; 23 PostgreSQL variants were skipped in the available environment. The exact-candidate natural guest journey used a running Gateway and real agent. A normal update retained [the original draft PR](https://github.com/shakkernerd/openclaw-guest-pr-demo/pull/19). After that owned fixture was intentionally closed, an explicit new request created [a separate draft PR](https://github.com/shakkernerd/openclaw-guest-pr-demo/pull/25), preserving the original closed head, saved checklist and branch history. Native receipts and independent GitHub readback agree; main stayed unchanged. The interruption cases use controlled external responses with production owners and real Git/SQLite. The live recordings cover the ordinary update and explicit-new-request controls; no live duplicate PR is claimed. The live capture is from `ceae6ae3`; the subsequent correction changes only the idle-recovery test fixture, with no runtime or UI changes. The inspected recordings and screenshots follow below. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Ordinary update after completion: baseline PR16 and candidate PR19 | ![Baseline ordinary update keeps draft PR16](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34098708-8936-4dc0-b34c-378d89030034) | ![Corrected candidate ordinary update keeps draft PR19](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6219e0f-fe8b-422b-80bd-7655c4f0d397) | | Before the explicit new request and after its result on ceae6ae3 | ![The composer contains an explicit request for a separate PR after closure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8c74437-33f6-4402-bbc4-8e981009caa5) | ![New draft PR25 is reported while original PR19 remains closed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ec7d9b9-e079-4e53-a02a-3c0c1340d8b4) | ### Two exact\-head controls; startup trimmed and agent wait periods visibly marked 4× https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c72a7253-4065-4dd2-9042-03095ebc3a49 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 4a5ec828b19c5207028faa9cdedb6528ae931c55 \(ordinary update\); ceae6ae3393032682788eea6d521970e547b80bb \(before the explicit new request\) - Exact head: `ceae6ae3393032682788eea6d521970e547b80bb` - Scenario: Ordinary controls on the exact corrected Gateway: update the original draft PR, then explicitly request a new draft after the owned original is intentionally closed\. The interruption itself is proven separately with controlled external responses and real Git/SQLite\. Baseline and candidate ordinary\-update images use independent owned fixtures; the explicit\-new before/after states are both on the corrected build\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.8\-ceae6ae33930\-2026\-10\-28T13\-57\-59\.273Z; bundled UI - Candidate outcome: Same PR19; one descendant commit; original body and main unchanged - Saved change: 13 added checklist lines; no deleted lines - Recording limits: Startup trimmed; full action/result retained; raw recording preserved - Original PR19: Closed, not merged; accepted b63a75a7 head and body unchanged - New PR25: Observed at capture: open draft at ba67f4f2, descended from the accepted update - Saved work and main: 10 added return\-handling lines, no deletions; main unchanged - Native publication receipts independently matched GitHub state and commit ancestry\. - Synthetic owned fixtures only; model controls hidden and media inspected\. - Controlled interruption is proven separately through production owners, real Git/SQLite and controlled GitHub responses; these captures show ordinary workflow controls\. - The original PR was intentionally closed through the approved test\-repo API between the two captures\. - The combined recording retains every rendered frame of both inspected component clips\. - Final PR head04df8fe1 changes only an idle\-recovery test fixture after captureheadceae6ae3; production and UI source are identical\.
